final_message:
The bug was in `collect` in `billing/payments.py`. When the gateway declined a charge, the failure branch was an empty `else: pass`. `record_failure` never ran, so the invoice's attempt count and retry time weren't updated and the subscription never went `past_due`. I replaced the `pass` with `record_failure(ctx, invoice, result["failure_code"] or "card_declined")`.

The full suite passes (25 tests) and mypy is clean. I added your test to `tests/test_lifecycle.py`. I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}`.

The `or "card_declined"` fallback is my addition. It covers a failed charge that comes back without a failure code.

steps.command: ls billing tests && wc -l billing/*.py && cat tests/conftest.py && grep -n "past_due\|retry\|def " billing/*.py | head -150
cat billing/dunning.py billing/payments.py && sed -n 30,110p billing/engine.py && grep -n "def transition" -A25 billing/subscriptions.py

python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/payments.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    else:\n        pass\n","    else:\n        record_failure(ctx, invoice, result[\"failure_code\"] or \"card_declined\")\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_lifecycle.py <<'E'


def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -3
